title: Finite coproducts of set sheaves are disjoint and universal
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] in a universe containing its objects and morphisms [def-weil-size-convention], and write $\mathcal E=\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ for its set-valued sheaves. Then $\mathcal E$ is finitary extensive: it has finite coproducts, its initial object $0$ is strict (every map to $0$ is an isomorphism), and finite coproducts are disjoint and universal. Explicitly, for any finite family $(A_i)_{i\in I}$ with coproduct $A=\coprod_{i\in I}A_i$, each inclusion $A_i\to A$ is monic, $A_i\times_A A_j\simeq0$ when $i\ne j$, and for every map $B\to A$ the canonical map $\coprod_{i\in I}(B\times_A A_i)\to B$ is an isomorphism.
